correctness.rationale: Each comparison has variance one quarter. Disjoint pair comparisons are independent, while the two shared-index orientations have joint probabilities one third and one sixth, giving covariances \(\pm1/12\); these are exactly the off-diagonal entries of \(B^\top B/12\). For the oriented incidence matrix, \(BB^\top=nI-J\), so \(Q=B^\top B\) satisfies \(Q^2=nQ\). Direct multiplication gives the proposed inverse, and the rank of \(B\) gives eigenvalue \(n\) of \(Q\) with multiplicity \(n-1\) and zero on the cycle space, yielding spectrum and determinant. Equal precision diagonals and the standard residual-correlation identity give \(\pm1/(n-1)\). An independent exact enumeration of small permutations in this audit matched the covariance identity. The packaged VERIFICATION.md was also inspected; its finite replay is supplementary to the analytic proof.
correctness.risk: The novelty lies in the complete probabilistic covariance/precision classification; the incidence-matrix algebra after recognizing \(C\) is classical.

value.rationale: Pairwise comparisons are the atomic variables behind inversion counts, Kendall-type statistics and permutation graphs. The theorem gives their complete finite second-order geometry and an unusual exact self-sparsity property: conditioning linearly on every other comparison creates no inverse-covariance fill-in. The cut/cycle spectrum and explicit residual correlations make this a natural reusable benchmark.
value.risk: Zero precision is only a linear partial-correlation statement and does not imply nonlinear conditional independence.

final_claim: For all inversion indicators of a uniform random permutation, with \(B\) the oriented complete-graph incidence matrix, the covariance is \(C=(I+B^\top B)/12\), the precision is \(12(I-B^\top B/(n+1))\), the spectrum and determinant have the stated two-level forms, and full-order linear partial correlations are zero for disjoint comparisons and \(\pm1/(n-1)\) for incident comparisons.
limitations: Uniform random permutations, equivalently iid continuous comparisons, only.
